01 — At a glance

Four numbers, one glance

The top of the page is a summary — everything else on the dashboard explains how these four were arrived at.

live screenshot
  • ValuePortfolio Value — total worth of everything you hold, in rupees. The sparkline is your real value trend; the % is the move since yesterday's close, weighted by how much of your money is in each stock.
  • TopTop Holding — your single largest position as a share of the whole portfolio. A quick concentration-risk check.
  • P&LUnrealized P&L — the profit or loss you'd lock in if you sold everything right now, at today's prices. "Unrealized" because you haven't actually sold.
  • IndexKSE-100 Index — Pakistan's headline market benchmark, sourced directly from PSX's own data portal, so you can see whether you're beating or trailing the broader market.

02 — Price Trends

Where the price has actually been

Not an animation — this is the real daily closing price for whichever stock (or the index) you have selected in the tabs.

live screenshot
  • TabsSwitch between the index and each stock you own. Each tab pulls its own real six-month price history.
  • SolidThe solid line is the closing price, trading day by trading day.
  • DashedThe dashed line is your own average buy rate. Price above it means that position is currently in profit; below it, it isn't.
  • HoverHover any point on the line for the exact price, the day's move, and how it compares to your buy price.

03 — Holdings

Everything you own, and what it's doing

One row per stock. Click a row to expand it.

live screenshot
  • RowCurrent value, its weight in your portfolio, profit/loss, and your average buy price.
  • BadgeThe colored chip next to each ticker — Buy / Hold / Sell — is today's technical signal for that stock. Same signal, same logic, as Market Signals below.
  • ExpandClick a row and it opens to show the full reasoning behind that signal, plus the option to remove the position.
Two of these five holdings (FNBM, SPEL) aren't on the 20-stock tracked list, so their badge only appears once Yahoo Finance actually has usable data for them.

06 — Taking action

This page decides what. Your broker executes it

PSX Portfolio never places an order — it's research. When you're ready to act, that happens on your actual broker terminal, ACPL's Web Trade Cast.

live screenshot · ACPL
  • WatchACPL's Market Watch is the live version of what our Market Signals list shows end-of-day — real-time Buy/Sell columns instead of a once-a-day close.
  • SpreadBefore acting on a Buy or Sell badge, check the live Buy/Sell price gap here. A wide spread means the price you'd actually get can differ from the last traded price.
  • DepthMBO/MBP (top right) is the order queue at each price level — a read on how easily your order size would actually fill.
  • OrderBuy Order / Sell Order (and the LB — limit — variants) is where the trade actually happens. This step has no equivalent on our page by design.
Our prices refresh from Yahoo Finance and PSX's Data Portal on a delay, not tick-by-tick. Always confirm the live price on ACPL before placing an order — treat our signal as the "why," not the fill price.

07 — Scenario

You don't own it yet — but Worth Investing In flags one

A concrete run-through of using both platforms together, start to finish.

PSX Portfolio ACPL Web Trade Cast
1AppOpen Worth Investing In and see, say, MLCF ranked with a Strong Buy — read the plain-English reasoning: RSI recovering from oversold, MACD just turned bullish, price back above its 50-day average.
2AppFlip to that stock's tab in Price Trends to see the last six months, not just today's reading — confirm the move isn't a one-day spike.
3ACPLSearch the symbol in Market Watch on Web Trade Cast. Compare the live LastPrice and the Buy/Sell spread to what you just saw — remember, the signal is a same-day read, not real-time.
4ACPLGlance at MBO/MBP for that symbol — the order queue at each price level gives a rough read on how easily your order size would fill.
5ACPLPlace a Buy Order — or an LB Buy Order if you'd rather set your own limit price than take the live offer.
6AppBack in PSX Portfolio, use the gear icon to Add Holding with your real fill price and quantity — this is what keeps your Portfolio Value, P&L, and the dashed avg-buy-rate line accurate from here on.

08 — Scenario

A holding you own turns Sell

The same two-platform pattern, running the other direction.

PSX Portfolio ACPL Web Trade Cast
1AppIn the Holdings table, a stock you own — say BAFL — now shows a Sell badge instead of the Hold it had last week.
2AppClick the row to expand it and read why: RSI has pushed into overbought territory, and price just closed below its 50-day average.
3AppCheck the Price Trends tab for BAFL — is the price still above your dashed avg-buy-rate line (you'd be selling at a profit) or below it (a loss)?
4ACPLOpen Market Watch and check the live Sell price for BAFL against what you'd actually be closing at right now.
5ACPLPlace a Sell Order — or an LB Sell Order — for some or all of the position. You don't have to exit the whole thing at once.
6AppUpdate the holding's quantity (or remove it entirely) back in PSX Portfolio so the dashboard reflects what you actually still own.
Selling only part of a position leaves your average buy rate unchanged for what's left — the dashed line on Price Trends won't move.

09 — Quick reference

Two things worth knowing

The two questions that come up most.

What Buy / Hold / Sell actually means

Five technical indicators are scored and summed — RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands, and two moving-average checks.

BUYMost indicators agree the stock is turning up. Strong Buy means all of them do.
HOLDIndicators are mixed — no clear direction either way right now.
SELLMost indicators agree the stock is turning down. Strong Sell means all of them do.
NOTEThis is a same-day read of price momentum — not a fundamentals, valuation, or news-driven call.

Physical vs CDC

The "Form" field on each holding — how the shares are actually held.

PhysicalOld-style paper share certificates. Transfer requires manual endorsement, and they're at real risk of loss, damage, or forgery.
CDCShares held electronically through PSX's Central Depository System. Instant transfer, no paper risk — what virtually every broker requires today.
NOTEIf you're not sure which yours are, they're almost certainly CDC unless you specifically hold old paper certificates.
